newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo invoiced 1.7 pct fewer cars in '96.
newsitem.headline: Volvo invoiced 1.7 pct fewer cars in '96.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo said on Tuesday the number of cars it invoiced in 1996 fell 1.7 percent to 368,300 vehicles.
Volvo said the year started weak, especially in Europe.
"The situation improved towards the end of the year, however, once the changeover to production of the Volvo S40/V40 had been completed," Volvo said in a statement.

Production of the S40/V40 model reached 71,000 units, which exceeded the planned 65,000. The year was also marked by strong sales in Japan, which increased 17 percent, and improved market shares in Japan and the U.S..
Volvo's market shares increased to 1.03 percent in 1996 from 1.01 percent the previous year in the U.S. and to 0.65 percent from 0.50 percent in Japan, Volvo said.
